chunks.title: [OLD MISCONCEPTION] Embedding Matrix W_E vs Input X & Fact Storage
chunks.content: Old Note (2026-11-03): I initially thought X in R^(T x d_model) was the entire dictionary W_E (thinking T = V) and that we could search factual company answers directly inside W_E.

chunks.title: [VALIDATED MASTERY] W_E vs Input X, Self-Attention (Q,K,V) & FFN World Memory
chunks.content: Validated Note (2026-11-06): W_E in R^(V x d_model) is the fixed Vocabulary Dictionary of V=128,256 isolated tokens. When a prompt of length T arrives, we pluck T rows from W_E to build the sentence matrix X in R^(T x d_model). Self-Attention (softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k) + M)V) computes token-to-token relationships inside X, while the Feed-Forward Network (FFN, ~75% of parameters) stores general world knowledge learned from pre-training. Private facts live outside the LLM in ChromaDB (RAG) or SQL (MCP).

chunks.title: LLM Inference Systems: Prefill (TTFT) vs Decode (TPS), KV-Cache & GQA
chunks.content: Prefill processes all T prompt tokens in parallel (Matrix-Matrix multiplication, Compute-bound, measured by TTFT). Decode generates tokens 1-by-1 auto-regressively (Vector-Matrix multiplication, Memory-Bandwidth bound, measured by TPS). KV-Cache saves past Keys and Values so Decode is O(t) instead of O(t^2), costing VRAM = 2 * L * H_kv * d_h * S * B * P. Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) shares 1 KV head across G Query heads, shrinking KV-Cache by 4x-8x.

chunks.title: Production RAG: Parent-Child Chunking, Unit L2 Normalization, HNSW, BM25+RRF, RAPTOR & GraphRAG
chunks.content: When vectors are L2-normalized (||u||=||v||=1), ||u-v||_2^2 = 2(1 - cos(theta)), so Dot Product, Cosine Similarity, and Euclidean L2 produce the exact same ranking (3x faster via Dot Product). ChromaDB uses HNSW (3-layer skip-list graph, O(log N)). Hybrid Search combines Dense Vector + BM25 via Reciprocal Rank Fusion RRF = 1/(60+rank_dense) + 1/(60+rank_bm25), followed by Cross-Encoder re-ranking. For massive datasets: RAPTOR builds a hierarchical summary tree by topic, whereas GraphRAG connects scattered entities across different documents via multi-hop edges.

chunks.title: Project: Databricks Smart Mobility Lakehouse & SQL/Python DE Mastery
chunks.content: Built end-to-end Medallion Architecture (Bronze raw -> Silver cleaned/deduplicated -> Gold KPIs) using PySpark and Delta Lake ACID transactions, guarded by pre-commit (ruff, mypy with explicit_package_bases) and GitHub Actions CI/CD. Mastered SQL logical execution order (FROM -> JOIN -> WHERE -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> SELECT -> DISTINCT -> ORDER BY -> LIMIT), conditional aggregation HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN...), and Python heapq K-way merge using tuple tie-breaking (value, stream_idx, iterator).

chunks.title: Computer Vision Foundations: 3D CNN Kernels, Spatial Formulas & ResNet Residual Skips
chunks.content: 3D CNN kernel volume (K x K x C_in), spatial output formula floor((W - K + 2P)/S) + 1, and parameter counting (K*K*C_in + 1)*C_out. ResNet residual skip connections y = F(x) + x resolve vanishing gradients across deep backbones.

chunks.content: RAPTOR Level-1 GenAI Summary: Complete mastery of Transformer math (W_E, RoPE, QKV Self-Attention, FFN memory, KV-Cache, GQA), Production RAG (ChromaDB HNSW, Hybrid BM25+RRF, Cross-Encoder, RAPTOR Tree, GraphRAG), MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 (`Host -> Client -> Server`), and Multi-Subagent Orchestration (`Code -> Test -> Review -> GitDeploy`) where evaluator retry loops boost 10-step reliability from 43.4% (0.92^10) to 99.49%.

chunks.content: FlashAttention fuses QK^T, softmax, and V multiplication inside fast on-chip GPU SRAM via online softmax tiling, avoiding O(T^2) HBM reads/writes.

chunks.title: Frontend Architecture: React Component Model, Hooks, Virtual DOM and Streaming UI
chunks.content: React builds declarative UIs where UI = f(state). Key rules: (1) Functional components with Hooks (useState for local state, useEffect for side-effects/API lifecycle with cleanup, useMemo/useCallback to prevent expensive re-renders, useRef for mutable DOM/stream references). (2) Virtual DOM reconciliation diffs component trees in O(N) using unique key props on lists. (3) For AI/LLM Full-Stack apps, connect React to backend streaming endpoints via Fetch ReadableStream or Server-Sent Events (SSE) for real-time token rendering.

chunks.title: Backend Choice: Node.js + Express vs. Python FastAPI and OWASP Web Security
chunks.content: Backend selection rule: (1) Choose Node.js + Express for I/O-heavy web gateways, BFF (Backend-For-Frontend), real-time WebSocket servers, session/cookie MVC apps (Project/myapp), or unified JS/TS stacks; Node.js uses the single-threaded non-blocking Libuv Event Loop to handle thousands of concurrent I/O connections. (2) Choose Python FastAPI (ASGI + Uvicorn + Pydantic v2) when the backend executes AI/ML inference (PyTorch, SentenceTransformers), RAG vector search (ChromaDB), or data pipelines (Project/historical-news-search, Project/shortest-link). Mandatory OWASP security: SQL prepared statements, Zod/Pydantic validation, CSP + output escaping (XSS), HttpOnly/SameSite cookies + CSRF tokens, and strict upload MIME whitelisting.

chunks.title: API Protocol Selection Matrix: REST vs. SSE vs. WebSockets vs. gRPC vs. MCP
chunks.content: Protocol choice by communication pattern: (1) REST (HTTP/JSON): Stateless CRUD over resource nouns (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), pagination, rate-limiting (429), and status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 422, 500). (2) Server-Sent Events (SSE): Unidirectional server-to-client HTTP stream; ideal for streaming LLM tokens to React. (3) WebSockets: Bidirectional full-duplex persistent TCP channel; ideal for live chat rooms and collaborative state. (4) gRPC (Protobuf/HTTP2): High-throughput binary microservice-to-microservice RPC. (5) MCP (JSON-RPC 2.0): Standardized AI Agent-to-Tool/DB protocol (@resource, @tool, @prompt).

chunks.title: Modern Python Toolchain: uv Package Manager, Ruff Linter/Formatter, Mypy and Pre-Commit
chunks.content: Production Python project setup (from uv-guide, ruff-guide, precommit-guide): (1) uv: Rust-powered package and virtualenv manager (10x-100x faster than pip/poetry); uses pyproject.toml + deterministic uv.lock, uv sync --frozen for reproducible builds, and uv run for zero-activation execution. (2) Ruff: Replaces Flake8, Black, and isort in one Rust binary (ruff check --fix for lint rules E/F/W/I/B/UP and ruff format). (3) Mypy: Static type checker (mypy --strict, explicit_package_bases = true) catching type/None bugs before runtime. (4) Pre-commit: Git hook manager (.pre-commit-config.yaml) running ruff, mypy, check-yaml, and trailing-whitespace before every git commit.

chunks.title: Containerization and CI/CD: Docker Multi-Stage Builds, Docker Compose and GitLab CI / GitHub Actions
chunks.content: Deployment and CI/CD Architecture (from gitlab-ci-guide and Project/shortest-link): (1) Docker: Multi-stage Dockerfiles (Stage 1 builder runs uv sync --frozen --no-dev or npm ci and npm run build; Stage 2 runtime copies built artifacts into python:3.11-slim or node:20-alpine as non-root user) with .dockerignore excluding .venv, node_modules, and .git. (2) Docker Compose (docker-compose.yml): Orchestrates multi-container stacks (React + Express/FastAPI + Postgres/ChromaDB/Redis) with healthchecks, volumes, and .env config. (3) GitLab CI/CD (.gitlab-ci.yml) and GitHub Actions: Automated 4-stage pipeline (lint -> test -> build -> deploy) with dependency caching so broken code never merges to main.

chunks.title: [RAPTOR Level-1 Summary] Full-Stack Web (React, Node/Express, FastAPI, APIs) and DevOps (uv, Ruff, Pre-Commit, Docker, CI/CD)
chunks.content: RAPTOR Level-1 Full-Stack and DevOps Decision Blueprint: Frontend in React (Hooks + SSE/REST); Backend in Node.js/Express (for I/O gateways, WebSockets, MVC sessions) or Python FastAPI (for AI/LLM/RAG/Data workloads); API layer via REST, SSE, WebSockets, or MCP; Code quality enforced via uv, ruff, mypy, pytest, and pre-commit; packaged via multi-stage Docker and docker-compose; and gated by GitLab CI/CD or GitHub Actions.

chunks.title: Classical Machine Learning and Tabular AI: Scikit-Learn, XGBoost, Cross-Validation and Leakage Prevention
chunks.content: Tabular ML Decision Rule (SY09): On structured/tabular datasets (<1M rows), Gradient Boosted Decision Trees (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) outperform Deep Learning. Core engineering rules: (1) Prevent Data Leakage by fitting StandardScaler, Imputer, and TargetEncoder strictly inside sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline on X_train only during Stratified K-Fold Cross-Validation. (2) Bias-Variance and Regularization: L1 (Lasso) induces sparsity for feature selection; L2 (Ridge) shrinks collinear weights; PCA/SVD projects orthogonal maximum-variance axes. (3) Class Imbalance: Use PR-AUC and F1/F-beta instead of ROC-AUC or accuracy; tune scale_pos_weight and probability thresholds. (4) Explainability: Use SHAP values for global and local feature attribution.

chunks.title: Deep Learning Architectures and Training: PyTorch, U-Net Segmentation, ResNet/ViT, AdamW and AMP
chunks.content: Deep Learning Architecture Selection (Project/U_net_ and CV): (1) Image Classification: ResNet50 (residual skip connections y = F(x) + x prevent vanishing gradients) or Vision Transformer (ViT). (2) Pixel-Level Semantic Segmentation (Medical/Industrial Microscopy): U-Net symmetric Encoder-Decoder with skip connections concatenating high-resolution encoder feature maps with upsampled decoder maps, trained with Dice Loss + Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE). (3) PyTorch Production Training Loop: optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) -> torch.amp.autocast(bf16/fp16) forward pass -> loss.backward() -> clip_grad_norm_ -> optimizer.step() with AdamW (decoupled weight decay) and Cosine Annealing LR with Warmup.

chunks.title: LLM Post-Training, Fine-Tuning and Serving: RAG vs. LoRA/QLoRA, DPO, Quantization and vLLM
chunks.content: Decision Rule (RAG vs. Fine-Tuning): Use RAG when facts change dynamically or require source citations; use Fine-Tuning (SFT + LoRA/QLoRA) when teaching domain tone, strict JSON/tool schemas, or distilling a large model into a fast 7B/8B model. LoRA Math: Freezes pretrained W_0 in R^(d x k) and trains low-rank delta W = W_0 + (alpha/r) * B * A where B in R^(d x r), A in R^(r x k) with rank r << min(d,k) (e.g., r=16), cutting trainable parameters by >99%. QLoRA quantizes W_0 to 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) with Double Quantization and Paged Optimizers. Alignment uses DPO (Direct Preference Optimization on chosen vs. rejected pairs without a separate Reward Model). Production serving uses vLLM (PagedAttention eliminating KV-Cache fragmentation) + AWQ/FP8 quantization.

chunks.title: Distributed Streaming Architecture: Apache Kafka Brokers, Partitions, Consumer Groups and Exactly-Once (Module 06)
chunks.content: Event-Driven Streaming (AI/Module_06): Choose Apache Kafka over REST/RabbitMQ for high-throughput, durable, replayable event logs and Change Data Capture (CDC). Core mechanics: (1) Topics are sharded into Partitions (the unit of parallelism); strict ordering is guaranteed ONLY within a single partition via hash(message_key) mod P. (2) Durability and Fault Tolerance: Leader + Follower replicas across Brokers with acks=all and min.insync.replicas=2. (3) Consumer Groups: Horizontal scaling where each partition is consumed by at most ONE consumer within a group (avoid having more consumers than partitions). (4) Delivery Semantics: At-Least-Once (commit offset after processing + idempotent sink) vs. Exactly-Once (transactional producer + read_committed).

chunks.title: PySpark Optimization, Kimball Star Schema (SCD Type 2), dbt and Unity Catalog Governance (Module 07 & NF26)
chunks.content: Data Engineering & Warehouse Core (AI/Module_07 and Project/NF26_Smart_Teems): (1) PySpark Tuning: Minimize Wide Transformations (Shuffle); use Broadcast Hash Join (broadcast(small_df)) when dimension table <100MB; resolve Data Skew via key salting or Adaptive Query Execution (AQE); optimize Delta Lake via OPTIMIZE + ZORDER BY on high-cardinality filter columns and VACUUM. (2) Data Modeling (Kimball Star Schema & dbt): Central Fact tables (granular measurements + foreign keys) surrounded by Dimension tables with SCD Type 2 (valid_from, valid_to, is_current) for historical tracking, built via modular dbt SQL layers (staging -> intermediate -> marts) and served to PowerBI. (3) Unity Catalog Governance: 3-level namespace (catalog.schema.table), Row-Level Security (RLS), Column Masking, and end-to-end lineage.

chunks.title: Distributed System Design and MLOps/LLMOps: Caching, Load Balancing, MLflow and Drift Monitoring (Module 08)
chunks.content: System Design & Production MLOps (AI/Module_08): (1) High Availability & Scaling: L7 Load Balancers, Consistent Hashing, Redis Caching (Cache-Aside with TTL + random jitter to prevent Cache Stampede / Thundering Herd), Database Read Replicas + Sharding, and CAP Theorem trade-offs. (2) Production MLOps & LLMOps: Experiment and model registry via MLflow, Feature Stores for online/offline parity, Statistical Drift Detection (Population Stability Index PSI and Kolmogorov-Smirnov test triggering automated retraining), and LLM Observability (tracing TTFT/TPS latency, token budgets, and online RAGAS faithfulness guardrails).

chunks.content:
# Advanced Fourier and Wavelet Transforms in AI Engineering

Mathematical foundations of continuous and discrete Fourier Transforms (FT, DFT, FFT) and Wavelet Transforms for signal, time-series, and spatial representation in deep neural networks.
Fourier decomposition expresses signals as linear combinations of orthogonal basis sinusoids:
$$X[k] = \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} x[n] e^{-i 2\pi k n / N}$$
Wavelet transforms overcome the uncertainty principle trade-off via multi-resolution time-frequency localization.

chunks.title: [ALGORITHMS] External Sorting & K-Way Merge with Min-Heap
chunks.content:
# External Sorting & K-Way Merge with Min-Heap

## 1. Problem Context & Asymptotics
When sorting datasets larger than available RAM (e.g. 100 GB log files on an 8 GB worker), External Merge Sort divides the data into $K$ sorted runs on disk, then performs a multi-way merge.

## 2. Min-Heap Optimal K-Way Merge
A direct sequential scan across $K$ files yields $O(N \cdot K)$ complexity. By maintaining a Min-Heap of size $K$:
- **Heap Element Tuple**: `(current_value, run_index)`
- **Initialization**: Insert the first element from each of the $K$ sorted runs: $O(K \log K)$.
- **Streaming Loop**:
  1. Pop the minimum value from the heap and write to output buffer.
  2. Read the next item from that specific `run_index` and push it to the heap ($O(\log K)$).
- **Total Time Complexity**: $O(N \log K)$, where $N$ is total elements across all runs.
- **Space Complexity**: $O(K)$ auxiliary memory in RAM.

## 3. High-Throughput Production Pattern
In Python, this is implemented natively via `heapq.merge(*iterables)` with generator expressions to avoid loading entire arrays into memory.

chunks.title: [SYSTEM_DESIGN] Consistent Hashing with Virtual Nodes in Distributed Systems
chunks.content:
# Consistent Hashing with Virtual Nodes in Distributed Systems

## 1. Problem Formulation
In a distributed caching or database system (e.g. Cassandra, DynamoDB, Memcached), traditional modulo hashing $H(key) \pmod N$ causes massive rehashing ($O(K)$ keys moved) when a node is added or removed, inducing severe cache stampedes.

## 2. Mathematical Definition
Consistent hashing maps both servers and keys onto a circular hash ring $[0, 2^{32} - 1]$ using a uniform hash function (e.g., MurmurHash3 or SHA-256):
$$\text{RingPosition} = H(x) \pmod{2^{32}}$$

When a key $k$ is queried, it moves clockwise until it finds the first node whose position is greater than or equal to $H(k)$:
$$\text{AssignedNode}(k) = \min \{ n \in \text{Nodes} \mid H(n) \ge H(k) \} \cup \{\min(\text{Nodes})\}$$

## 3. Virtual Nodes (V-Nodes) for Load Balance
To avoid hot spots and non-uniform clustering on the ring, each physical node is replicated as $V$ virtual nodes:
- Physical server $S_i$ is mapped to $\{H(S_i \# 1), H(S_i \# 2), \dots, H(S_i \# V)\}$.
- Standard recommendation: $V \approx 100\text{--}256$ virtual nodes per physical host.
- When server $S_i$ crashes, its keys are evenly distributed across all remaining servers rather than overloading a single neighbor.

chunks.title: [MACHINE_LEARNING] Leak-Free Machine Learning Pipeline: HistGradientBoostingRegressor & Out-of-Fold Preprocessing
chunks.content:
# Leak-Free Machine Learning Pipeline: HistGradientBoostingRegressor & Out-of-Fold Preprocessing

## Core Principles
1. **Target Transformation**:
   In skewed price/valuation regression, apply `y_trans = log1p(y)` prior to fitting. The inverse transform `expm1(y_pred)` recovers true scale while optimizing for relative percentage error (RMSLE).

2. **Preventing Data Leakage**:
   All imputers, standardizers, and one-hot encoders must be fitted strictly on the training fold within a Scikit-Learn `Pipeline`. Fitting transformers on the full dataset before cross-validation produces optimistic test metric contamination.

3. **HistGradientBoosting vs XGBoost**:
   `HistGradientBoostingRegressor` discretizes continuous variables into 256 integer bins (histogram-based), reducing computation time from $O(N \cdot M)$ to $O(\text{bins} \cdot M)$ with native support for categorical features and missing values.
